name: Dinas Vawr
text: Dinas Vawr is an anglicized rendering of a fortress of pretended historicity. It was dreamed up by Thomas Love Peacock. Peacock coined the name for his comic novel The Misfortunes of Elphin, which appeared in 1829. Inside the novel stands a poem, The War-Song of Dinas Vawr. It celebrates Welshmen's joy in lifting sheep from neighbouring pastures. Set later to music, the piece has acquired almost the standing of a folk-song. Peacock offers no Welsh original. The implied form is dinas fawr, or mawr, meaning big fort. The spelling Dinas Vawr is therefore a literary jest rather than a real archaeological site.

okr.objective: Dinas Vawr as Peacock's fictitious Welsh fortress from The Misfortunes of Elphin.
